Right-biased and left-biased U.S. news outlets differ in their coverage of Discrimination & Toxicity AI risks in terms of the focus and language used. Right-biased outlets (36.1% of their articles) emphasize risks related to the false portrayal of historical figures, such as "the founding fathers as people of color," and express concerns about AI systems like ChatGPT producing responses that are perceived as biased against conservatives. They also highlight issues related to "bias in content moderation systems," where negative comments about women are flagged more often than similar comments about men.

In contrast, left-biased outlets (24.9% of their articles) report on risks associated with the inclusion of far-right and non-reputable sources in AI training data, which can lead to the dissemination of hate speech. They also focus on the negative impacts of AI technologies on marginalized groups, such as financial discrimination against people of color due to biased algorithms.

The language used in right-biased reporting tends to include politicized markers that align with their agenda, while left-biased reporting also employs politicized language but focuses on the implications of AI for social justice and the experiences of marginalized communities.
